You will provide advice to management on the evaluation of the effectiveness of the administrative support services and systems as well as oversee all administrative requirements for SWS program support.
You will on a daily basis utilize office automated systems, networks and software to manage, administer and maintain data.
You will track and compile various types of information for internal and external reports, metrics and data calls.
You will work closely with the Directorate Management Analyst to stay aware of ongoing efforts and help assist.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-09) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector as a Management Analyst.

Specialized experience must demonstrate: 1) Reviewing financial documents and records to ensure proper use, accounting, and reporting of funds. 2) Preparing financial status reports and budget analyses for management. 3) Performing personnel actions in accordance with applicable personnel policies. 4) Administering or coordinating monetary and time-off awards programs.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Duties for the Program Analyst position include, but are not limited to, the following: Using qualitative and quantitative analysis methods to analyze program-related data and to identify and analyze program or policy issues.

Providing operational, technical, and administrative support to critical projects, programs, and policies within the organization. Providing analytical techniques for evaluating the accomplishment of program objectives.

Assisting with drafting, reviewing, editing, and providing input to written materials including program guidance, and informational and decision memoranda. Designing statistically valid surveys, questionnaires, and data analysis techniques to evaluate programs.
Specialized Experience is the experience that equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities (KSA's) to perform the duties of the position successfully, and that is typically in or related to the position to be filled.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the next lower grade level. Applicants must have 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, GS-12, in the Federal Service.

Qualifying specialized experience for the GS-13 includes: Assisting with technical support and/or written communications directly relating to OSHA's state plans and/or OSHA's Office of State Programs.

Using OSHA Information System (OIS) and/or the State Plan Application (SPA) to analyze data directly relating to OSHA State Plans and their performance. Providing written responses to questions regarding policies, operations or administration of State Plans.

Serving as a Management Analyst GS-0343-9/11 makes you a valuable member of the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) team and mission. This position is located in the Core Training Operations Directorate under the Office of the Associate Director for Training Operations.

The primary purpose of this position is to provide analysis and administrative support. Typical duties include: Performing in-depth analysis of sensitive and complex administrative issues affecting the office, develops solutions, and implements new or modified guidelines to address operational challenges and enhance mission effectiveness.

Serving as the directorate-level point of contact for documentation management, leading the coordination, organization, and optimization of documentation workflows across platforms such as SharePoint, Internet, and Intranet, ensuring secure and efficient storage, retrieval, and lifecycle management.

Providing expert guidance and training to managers and staff on documentation management tools, procedures, and best practices, and resolves issues related to system use, documentation processes, and compliance with organizational policies.

Participating in strategic long-range planning, reviews and evaluates reports and correspondence for leadership, and assists with the preparation and quality control of directorate documentation, ensuring consistency, clarity, and alignment with administrative and policy requirements.

A resume must be no more than two pages. If an applicant's resume exceeds two pages, the USAJOBS database will not allow the application to be submitted.

For additional assistance, please visit: USAJOBS Help Center - Update your resume now so it meets new resume requirements Specialized Experience at the GS-09: You qualify at the GS-09 grade level if you possess one of the following: One year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-07 grade level in Federal service, or equivalent experience in the private or public sector that demonstrates the ability to: (1) Assist, analyze and find resolution of administrative issues, reviewing and preparing documents for accuracy and compliance, supporting office documentation management using electronic systems, and providing administrative support in timekeeping, travel, procurement, and property management.

(2) Coordinates with staff and partners to resolve routine issues, prepares presentations and reports, and uses office automation software to generate documents and improve workflows.

OR A master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related; OR A combination of successfully completed graduate level education and specialized experience as described above that, when combined, equal 100% of the total requirement.

This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application. NOTE: Only graduate education in excess of the first year may be used to qualify for the GS-09 level.

Specialized Experience at the GS-11:You qualify at the GS-11 grade level if you possess one of the following: One year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-09 grade level in Federal service, or equivalent experience in the private or public sector that demonstrates the ability to: (1) Independently resolve complex administrative issues, develop and implement policies and procedures, and managing documentation workflows using electronic systems (e.g., SharePoint).

(2) Provides guidance to management and staff, conducts research to support strategic planning and operational improvements, and prepares briefings and reports for leadership.

(3) Delivers training on administrative processes, oversees timekeeping, travel, procurement, and property management, and coordinates with stakeholders to address mission-related administrative matters.; OR A Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related; OR A combination of successfully completed graduate level education and specialized experience as described above that, when combined, equal 100% of the total requirement.

This will be calculated using your resume and unofficial transcripts or a list of courses/course hours submitted with your application. NOTE: Only graduate education in excess of the first two years may be used to qualify for the GS-11 level. All qualifications and eligibility requirements must be met by the closing date of the announcement.

Time-in-grade: Current General Schedule (GS) federal employees, and those that have served in GS positions within the last 52 weeks, must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade, or a combination of the next lower grade level and an equivalent band in the federal service by the closing of this announcement.

Note: Current or former Federal employees MUST submit a copy of their SF-50 Form which shows competitive service appointment ("position occupied" block 34 on the SF-50 should show a "1"), tenure group (block 24 should show a 1 or 2), grade, and salary.

If you are applying for a higher grade, please provide the SF-50 Form which shows the length of time you have been in your current/highest grade (examples of appropriate SF-50s include promotions, With-in Grade/Range Increases, and SF-50s dated a year apart within the same grade/job).

If you have promotion potential in your current position, please provide proof. Employees applying with an interchange agreement must provide proof of their permanent appointment. IF YOU DO NOT SUBMIT ALL OF THE REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION, YOU WILL NOT RECEIVE CONSIDERATION AS A STATUS CANDIDATE.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office.

Career Transition Assistance Program/Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP/ICTAP) Eligibles: If you have never worked for the federal government, you are not CTAP/ICTAP eligible. View information about CTAP/ICTAP eligibility on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.

In addition, you must submit the supporting documents listed under the "Required Documents" section of this announcement. This position may be filled at the GS-9 or GS-11 level.

If selection is made at the GS-9 level, promotion to the GS-11 level may occur without further competition. Background Investigation: To ensure the accomplishment of our mission, FLETC requires every employee to be reliable and trustworthy.

To meet those standards, all selected applicants must undergo and successfully pass a background investigation for suitability as a condition of placement in this position.

This review may include financial issues such as delinquency in the payment of debts, child support and/or tax obligations, as well as certain criminal offenses and illegal use or possession of drugs.

Duties may include but are not limited to: Serves as an on-site management representative for the Community-Based Outpatient Clinic, overseeing daily operations to ensure efficient patient flow, effective use of resources, and adherence to established clinical, administrative, and organizational processes.

Provides operational oversight and coordination across clinic functions, helping ensure that patient care delivery, front-line administrative activities, provider support, and clinic workflows are aligned with facility expectations and access-to-care goals.

Coordinates space planning, facility maintenance concerns, equipment requests, supply needs, and logistical support to promote a safe, functional, and efficient care environment for Veterans, staff, and visitors.

Fosters solid relationships by keeping staff members informed, being responsive to their requests, and obtaining information and expertise to present on specific issues and programs.

Conducts periodic reviews and analysis of issues and the systems associated with those issues that have come forward from Veterans and their family members and presents that information, along with recommended programmatic change, to the Medical Center Director and the Executive Board.

Collects and analyzes administrative and performance data including workload, access metrics, productivity, and resource utilization.

Ensures that CBOC operations are conducted in accordance with established clinical, administrative, safety, privacy, and information security requirements, helping maintain consistency between the CBOC and parent facility expectations.

Compiles summary and executive level reports related to the program; provides guidance to medical staff and other providers regarding pending and completed actions by major program. Addresses escalated Veteran concerns and ensures appropriate documentation and follow-through.

To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 08/05/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

For a GS-12 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-11. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials.

If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade.

Note: Time-In-Grade requirements also apply to former Federal employees applying for reinstatement as well as current employees applying for Veterans Employment Opportunities Act of 1998 (VEOA) appointment.

You may qualify as described below: Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-11 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: Academic foundation or vast experience in program management, some clinical experience or education/training in the ambulatory or inpatient setting, customer relations management, and healthcare operations in the public and private sectors.

You will be rated on the following Competencies for this position: Accountability Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Flexibility Influencing/Negotiating Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Learning Reading Comprehension Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religions; spiritual; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Note: A full year of work is considered to be 35-40 hours of work per week.

Part-time experience will be credited on the basis of time actually spent in appropriate activities. Applicants wishing to receive credit for such experience must indicate clearly the nature of their duties and responsibilities in each position and the number of hours a week spent in such employment.

Physical Requirements: Work is primarily sedentary with intermittent walking or standing. This position work site may be located from the Main Greater Los Angeles Campus, and driving will be required to the work site at which the position is responsible.

General Manager Duties: As a Front Line Manager you will: Plan work to be accomplished by subordinates, sets and adjusts short-term priorities and prepares schedules for completion of work. Assign work to subordinates based on priorities, selective consideration of the difficulty and requirements of assignments, and the capabilities of employees.

Evaluate work performance of subordinates and makes recommendations for outstanding performance recognition and/or disciplinary action. Give advice, counsel or instruction to employees on work and administrative matters.

Interview candidates for positions within the organization/unit and recommend appointment, promotion or reassignment to such positions. Hear and resolve complaints from employees, refer group grievances and/or more serious unresolved complaints as appropriate.

Effect minor disciplinary measures, such as warnings and reprimands, recommend other actions in more serious cases. Identify developmental and training needs of employees, providing or arranging for needed development and training. Initiate ways to improve production, work processes and/or to increase the quality of the work directed.

Provides leadership and direction for planning, administering, and evaluating assigned FMSS programs, projects, and organizational activities to ensure alignment with IRS and Department of the Treasury missions, goals, and strategic priorities.

Identifies, acquires, and allocates resources; establishes organizational priorities; manages budgetary and staffing requirements; and evaluates program effectiveness to ensure the efficient and effective delivery of products and services.

Directs staff in identifying, distributing, and balancing workload based on organizational priorities, mission requirements, workflow demands, and employee skill levels.

Establishes performance expectations, performance measures, and accountability standards for subordinate staff and organizational programs; provides guidance and feedback on work products; evaluates organizational performance; and ensures quality control, stewardship, and oversight of assigned programs, funding, contracts, and related activities.

Holds subordinate employees accountable for accomplishing assigned work, meeting performance expectations, achieving organizational objectives, adhering to established policies and procedures, and producing timely, accurate, and high-quality work products.

STANDARD POSITION DESCRIPTIONS (SPD): PD26412 Visit the IRS SPD Library to access the position descriptions.
Federal experience is not required. Experience may have been gained in the public sector, private sector or through Volunteer Service. One year of experience refers to full-time work; part-timework is considered on a prorated basis.

To ensure full credit for your work experience, please indicate dates of employment by month/day/year, and indicate number of hours worked per week, on your resume. You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: You must have one (1) year of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the next lower level within the payband or GS grade in the normal line of progression in the Federal service that demonstrates the required managerial skills and technical competence required to perform the job.

To be qualified for this position your experience must include: Experience that demonstrated management/leadership experience such as applying management techniques, methods, theories, principles, or labor relations concepts for the accomplishment of all program objectives with combined technical and administrative oversight.

This experience may have been gained through work experience as a project/program manager, team lead or project/program lead, technical advisor, or senior specialist/analyst that included managing resources, providing support to managers, mentoring team members, providing day-to-day guidance training and/or oversight of peers or others.

Experience applying regulations, other official guidance and principles, including the latest procedures and techniques sufficient to oversee the planning, development and implementation of the technical aspects of programs specific to the position being filled.

Experience applying communicative techniques to effectively and diplomatically interact with internal and external customers. Experience managing programs or organizational initiatives by establishing priorities, allocating resources, monitoring progress, and evaluating results to accomplish organizational goals.

Experience leading projects through planning, execution, monitoring, and completion while managing people, timelines, resources, risks, and project requirements. Experience developing and implementing process improvements, operational changes, and/or organizational solutions to address program challenges and improve performance.

Experience analyzing operational, financial, performance, and/or program data to identify trends, assess risks, evaluate organizational performance, and develop recommendations for management decision-making and process improvement.

Experience creating reports, analyses, recommendations, or decision documents to communicate program results and support management decision-making. Experience leading teams, working groups, and/or collaborative initiatives to resolve issues and accomplish program or project objectives.

AND You must also meet the following requirement(s): TIME AFTER COMPETITIVE APPOINTMENT (TACA): By the closing date (or if this is an open continuous announcement, by the cut-off date) specified in this job announcement, current civilian employees must have completed at least 90 days of federal civilian service since their latest non-temporary appointment from a competitive referral certificate, known as time after competitive appointment.

For this requirement, a competitive appointment is one where you applied to and were appointed from an announcement open to "All US Citizens". For more information on qualifications please refer to OPM's Qualifications Standards. Go to Understanding the IRS Paybands for GS/IR conversion.

As a Supply Systems Analyst, GS-2003-09, you will perform the below duties: Reviews, analyzes, and interprets supply directives and procedures. Formulates and recommends operating procedures to achieve optimum support to the logistics program on matters pertaining to property accountability.

Develops and provides data for property accountability of supported units/activities to the Supply Management Officer (SMO), Director of Logistics (DOL), United States Property and Fiscal Officer (USP&FO) and the Readiness Committee.

Is responsible for the serialization program for Controlled Cryptographic Items Serialization Program (CCISP), Small Arms Serialization Program (SASP), and Radiation Testing and Tracking System (RATTS) for the USP&FO. Serves as State Serialization Coordinator.

Is responsible for the State STAMIS Catalog Data File, State Assigned Line Item Number (SLIN) and non-expendable Management Control Numbers (MCN). Coordinates the Department of Defense Acquisition Activity Code (DODAAC) program for the state.

Is responsible for branch logistical support program to ensure units/activities receive guidance and assistance required to correct problems and deficiencies. Analyzes recommendations and issues written or verbal instructions to insure units achieve maximum readiness posture.

Coordinates work with unit/activity representatives concerning priorities, procedures and work accomplishment. Directs and publishes procedures to unit/activity representatives for implementation/update of property management Standard Army Management Information System (STAMIS).

Directs and provides written technical guidance to unit/activity representatives involving property book procedures and functions. Analyzes results of property book reconciliations to determine if systemic problems exist. Analyze trends for effectiveness and efficiency.

Conducts appropriate follow-up to assure deficiencies are corrected to improve undesirable conditions and accountability of equipment. Prepares budget estimates for Military Table of Equipment/Table of Distribution & Allowances (MTOE/TDA) change considerations.

Coordinates with Army Material Command (AMC), Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) and National Guard Bureau (NGB) program managers to effect receipt of required equipment to support readiness objectives. Acts as the Total Package Fielding (TPF) manager for the USP&FO. Coordinates incoming major end items to support readiness objectives.

Coordinates system administration for the property management branch to include STAMIS security, software and hardware changes. Participates with supervisor in carrying out the supervisory responsibilities of the Branch. Prepares requests for filling vacancies or for additional personnel to meet workload requirements.

Participates in the selection of subordinates from lists of eligible candidates. Participates in the setting of performance standards and in the evaluation of employee performance. Prepares formal requests and recommendations for promotions, reassignments, etc. Recommends recognition for outstanding performance.

Provides initial approval/disapproval of leave. Receives and resolves or participates in the resolution of grievances, or forwards to higher level management for resolution. Acts to resolve disciplinary problems, or forwards to higher management for resolution. Formulates plans for employee development for supervisor's approval.

Implements specific and general provisions of programs for equal treatment of all employees. Participates in applying position management principles and in insuring the accuracy of position descriptions.

Informs employees of all aspects of personnel programs of the installation, either answering routine questions or obtaining information from specialists when more technical answers are required. Performs other related duties as assigned.
NOTE: Qualifications are based on breadth/level of experience. In addition to describing duties performed, applicants must provide the exact dates of each period of employment (from MM/DD/YY to MM/DD/YY) and the number of hours worked per week if part time.

GENERAL EXPERIENCE: Applicant must have experience, education, or training which has provided the applicant with a general knowledge of one or more aspects of the supply field.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicant must have at least 12 months of specialized experience, equivalent to at least the GS-07 level, or equivalent pay band in other pay systems in the Federal government? This experience may also have been obtained in the private sector but must demonstrate that it is comparable to the GS grade indicated.

This experience must include activities such as: Experience analyzing, developing, evaluating to improve supply programs, policies, procedures, techniques, etc. Experience involving the control of supply stocks and accounting for equipment. Knowledge of supply functions, cataloging, maintenance, and disposal procedures.

Experience conducting extensive searches for required information; reconstruct records for complex supply transactions; and/or provide supply operations support.

As a Management Analyst, you will: Orchestrate Agency-Wide Strategic Plans - Help chart our collective path forward. You will play a key role in developing and updating high-level strategies across critical BPA departments-including Information Technology, Human Resources, Safety, Security, and Supply Chain.

Your work will directly support subject matter experts in modernizing operational policies to keep BPA agile. Drive Process Modernization and Efficiency - Champion continuous improvement. You will analyze existing workflows, staffing structures, and management practices to identify and resolve organizational bottlenecks.

By researching industry best practices and introducing modern technological solutions, you will design leaner, smarter processes that maximize BPA's resources. Lead Projects from Conception to Delivery - Own your projects end-to-end. You will define project scope, build realistic schedules, manage resources, and mitigate risks.

As a trusted project leader, you will present progress briefings directly to senior leadership and executives, ensuring your projects deliver exceptional results on time. Direct Crucial Vendor Partnerships - Maximize the value of our external contracts.

In this role, you will quickly secure your certification to serve as a Contracting Officer's Representative (COR). You will oversee contractor performance, ensure deliverables meet high-quality standards, keep projects on budget, and protect BPA from financial waste.

Establish Modern Performance Metrics and Evaluation Tools - Define what success looks like. You will collaborate with management to design clear business metrics and performance targets.

By identifying operational trends, you will construct innovative ways to measure program effectiveness, setting a brand-new precedent for how BPA evaluates its achievements. Negotiate and Collaborate Across BPA and DOE - Represent our team on the broader stage.

You will participate in agency-wide and Department of Energy (DOE) committees to tackle complex operational challenges. Acting as a technical expert, you will guide discussions, build consensus, and clearly communicate BPA's strategic position to diverse stakeholders.
SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-11) in the Federal service.

Specialized experience for this position is defined as experience 1) conducting, planning, and organizing projects and analytical studies of considerable scope to evaluate and recommend methods for improving program efficiency, organizational structures, and business metrics; and 2) managing a full range of project activities similar to those of a Contracting Officer Representative (COR), such as establishing project schedules and deliverables, coordinating resources, monitoring contractor performance, and providing advice to program managers.

"Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Leads planning, directing, coordinating, and supervising administrative and staff functions for a Storage and Distribution branch.
Oversee review and analysis, resource management, internal controls, personnel services, forms and publications, equipment, supplies, vehicle monitoring, and inter-service support agreements.
Supervises delivery, receipt, storage, and distribution of DLA and service-owned material, including non-standard specialized items.
Plans, establishes, and manages efficient and economical programs such as Quality Control, Document Processing, Inventory Accuracy, Accountability, and Stock Readiness.
Analyzes operations and recommends improvements by adapting existing or new technology to inventory and material storage systems at branch and regional levels.
Conducts research and analysis using DSS, management information systems, automated supply systems, computer applications, principles, and techniques.

You will serve as Deputy Chief of Staff responsible for management of Research and Development Support Activity (RDSA) personnel, facilities, and corporate management functions.
You will be responsible for the synchronization and integration of efforts across the organization, including management of all civilian, military, and contractor personnel.
You will coordinate with the Chief Human Capital Officer, Military Manpower Officer, and Contracting Officer's Representatives (COR) for the assimilation of information on hiring status and strategy for all personnel.
You will develop the strategic facility plan for Research and Development Support Activity (RDSA) facilities in the DC metro area and serve as the senior official for the RDSA headquarters facility.
You will support the Chief of Staff in development, justification, and execution of a multimillion dollar operating budget.
You will provide guidance, resources, and set priorities on the development of enterprise level business products to ensure effective and timely implementation.
You will perform the full breadth of supervisory duties to include: planning work, providing advice, hearing/resolving complaints, arranging developmental training, improving work/production quality, and developing/evaluating performance standards.
You will aid in building effective teams, fostering a culture of respect for all team members, and providing opportunities for professional development.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the next lower grade level (GG/GS-14) or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector, such as: 1.

Briefing and advising senior leaders in providing direction and decision making to maintain efficient and productive operations. 2.

Coordinating with organization leadership and Contracting Officer's Representatives (COR) for the assimilation of information on hiring status and manpower strategy for all civilian, military, and contractor personnel. 3. Coordinating with the organization's stakeholders to develop clear and accurate enterprise level support goals. 4.

Providing guidance, resources, and setting priorities on the development of enterprise level business products to ensure effective and timely implementation. 5. Building effective teams, fostering a culture of respect for all team members, and providing opportunities for professional development. 6.

Capturing facility requirements to develop a strategic facility plan that anticipates future needs and serving as the senior official for a facility.

As a Management Analyst (Grant Compliance Specialist) you will: Assist with the administration of the full grants life cycle by reviewing and processing award actions, post-award modifications, closeout activities, recipient submissions, and administrative documentation to ensure compliance with Federal regulations, HHS policy, and agency requirements.

Conducts analyses of grants, financial, and operational information; reviews budgets, reports, and resource plans; identifies compliance issues and discrepancies; and prepares findings and recommendations that support effective program and resource.

Assists in developing program plans, standard operating procedures, guidance documents, and administrative processes that improve efficiency, strengthen internal controls, and support effective program administration.

Advises Federal staff, grantees, and program officials on administrative and grants management requirements, coordinates activities across organizations, supports special projects, and prepares reports and briefing materials for management.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Minimum Qualifications: You must have one year specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-9 grade level in the Federal service performing or ALL of the following: Administering grants throughout the award life cycle in accordance with Federal policies and regulations.

Position Overview: The Senior Compliance Systems Analyst supports compliance-related system and process initiatives by serving as the day-to-day subject matter resource for assigned regulatory areas.

This role is responsible for evaluating regulatory requirements, conducting first-pass research and analysis, helping design how requirements should function within the loan origination system and related workflows, and supporting the implementation of compliance-related changes.

This role serves as a compliance subject-matter expert for designated LOS functionality, helping to establish, maintain, and continuously improve system behavior in alignment with regulatory requirements and internal policies.

The Senior Compliance Systems Analyst operates at a level above pure testing execution by owning assigned workstreams, drafting and refining requirements, coordinating with stakeholders, and helping move changes from analysis through implementation and validation.

This role partners closely with Legal, Technology, Operations, and Compliance leadership to ensure requirements are translated into practical, compliant business and system behavior. Job Responsibilities:
· Serve as the primary compliance subject matter resource for assigned regulatory areas (for example, TILA, RESPA, TRID, and the SAFE Act, among others) and act as the day-to-day owner of related analysis, requirements, testing support, and implementation activities.
· Evaluate regulatory requirements, investor guidance, overlays, and internal policy expectations to determine how they should be reflected in loan origination system functionality, operational workflows, disclosures, documents, and related controls.
· Conduct first-pass regulatory research and issue analysis, identify open questions or gray areas, and prepare work products for attorney or executive compliance review and sign-off.
· Translate regulatory and business requirements into clear business, system, and procedural requirements that Technology, Operations, and other stakeholders can understand and execute.
· Help design how regulatory requirements should function within the loan origination system, including rules, fields, logic, workflows, outputs, and related operational impacts.

Foundever 's NSOS Operational Efficiency team is scaling its Bill-to-Pay (BTP) Margin Recovery initiative — a structured analytical programme that identifies where Gross Margin (GM) is being lost at the account level and turns those findings into operational actions that drive measurable GM improvement across the EMEA region.
We are hiring a Business Analysts to extend coverage across the EMEA portfolio, supporting our goal of reviewing 50 accounts by the end of H2 2026.
The core of the role is a repeatable four-step process: (1) build an optimal BTP baseline for each account using financial performance data; (2) diagnose the gaps between that baseline and actual operational results, quantifying the GM opportunity by root cause; (3) translate findings into clear, prioritized recommendations and hand them off to Operations or Account Management for execution; and (4) track the evolution of each gap month-over-month to measure whether corrective actions are closing the performance shortfall.
You will not own the execution of corrective actions — that responsibility sits with Operations. Your role is to be the analytical engine behind the initiative: detecting, quantifying, communicating, and monitoring until each gap is resolved or escalated.

BTP Analysis & Gap Detection
For each assigned account, build a BTP baseline from financial performance data and WFM inputs to establish the optimal labour cost scenario.
Compare the optimal scenario based on the assumptions used for pricing against actual results (Theoretical Production, Actual, and Invoiced) to identify and size performance gaps by root cause: e.g. unplanned absenteeism, non-productive time, scheduling adherence failures, unbillable hours cap impact, internal shrinkage deviations, etc
Quantify the GM opportunity associated with each gap driver, at both the individual account level and aggregated across the portfolio.
Maintain a throughput of approximately 10 account analyses per Business Analyst every two weeks, consistent with the team's EMEA scaling roadmap.
Findings Communication & Operational Handoff
Translate analytical findings into structured, prioritized output (findings, root causes, recommended actions, estimated GM impact) formatted for handoff to Operations and Account Management.
Present conclusions clearly to non-technical stakeholders, focusing on the 'so what' — what needs to change, who owns it, and what the financial benefit of closing the gap is.
Coordinate with Operations and Account Management to validate findings and ensure recommended actions are operationally feasible before sign-off.
Monthly Follow-Up & Evolution Tracking
For accounts in active monitoring, track month-over-month BTP performance versus the established baseline to assess whether corrective actions are delivering the expected improvement.
Identify root-cause gaps that are improving, stagnating, or worsening, and escalate unresolved or recurring issues to the Director of Operational Efficiency with supporting evidence.
Maintain updated account records that document gap status, action ownership, and GM impact realised to date.
Process Consistency
Apply the team's standardized BTP methodology consistently across all assigned accounts and countries, ensuring comparability of findings across the EMEA portfolio.
Flag where data availability, data quality, or system limitations are constraining analysis accuracy, and contribute to the team's ongoing effort to improve data access and analytical automation.
What you need in order to be successful

2–4 years of experience in business analysis, workforce management analytics, financial operations analysis, or a related field — ideally within a BPO, contact center, or outsourced services environment.
Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Industrial Engineering, Economics, Statistics, or a related discipline (or equivalent practical experience).
Proven experience working with financial performance data (P&L, margin, cost of labour) and operational metrics to generate actionable insight.
Technical Skills
Advanced Excel skills: structured analysis, financial modelling, pivot tables, formulas.
Solid understanding of workforce management concepts: shrinkage (internal and external), AUX/activity codes, scheduling adherence, login compliance, billable vs. paid hours.
Ability to work with WFM platform data exports (e.g. IEX) and account-level financial performance reports to build and validate BTP scenarios.
Comfortable working with incomplete, inconsistent, or manually compiled source data — able to apply structured judgement to reconcile discrepancies and document assumptions.
Soft Skills
Strong analytical and root-cause-diagnosis mindset: able to move from a raw dataset to a clear, prioritized narrative about where margin is being lost and why.
Excellent written and verbal communication in English; able to present complex financial and operational findings to non-technical stakeholders without requiring translation.
Organized and accountable: comfortable managing a recurring portfolio of accounts on a fixed monthly cadence, with clear documentation of status and progress.
Collaborative and assertive: able to work with Operations and Account Management to validate and land recommendations, without assuming ownership of their execution.
Languages
Fluent English required (written and spoken) — primary language for all reporting and stakeholder communication.
Additional French is a plus.
The work environment
A central role in a EMEA COO-sponsored, high-visibility initiative with direct, measurable impact on EMEA Gross Margin performance.
Exposure to senior cross-functional stakeholders across Operations, Account Management, and Finance.
A structured methodology to work within, with scope to help shape the team's evolution toward data automation and scalable analytics.
Career development within a growing analytics function at one of the world's leading customer experience companies.

At JetBrains, code is our passion. Ever since we started, back in 2000, we have strived to make the strongest, most effective developer tools on earth. By automating routine checks and corrections, our tools speed up production, freeing developers to grow, discover, and create.
The Business Application Development team builds and supports internal and customer-facing systems for licenses, subscriptions, billing, payments, reporting, and many other business-critical functions. Our domain is complex, our systems are interconnected, and there’s always a lot going on. We’re seeking a Senior Business Analyst to join the team and support our efforts.
We’re not looking for someone who will just write requirements. We want someone who likes digging into problems, understanding how things actually work, talking to people, asking uncomfortable questions, and helping teams move toward practical and sustainable solutions.

You’ll work closely with stakeholders, developers, and QA engineers, as well as sales, customer success, and other product teams, to figure out what problem we’re really solving, why it matters, what constraints exist, and what solution makes the most sense long term.
A core responsibility is helping people stay focused on the actual goal instead of jumping straight to a “we need this exact feature” reaction. Though sometimes bigger, the right solution is often smaller than originally expected. The main job is frequently untangling the chaos and helping everyone align.
Organize and improve the intake and analysis process within the team.

s.h: Structure requirements to support effective development.
s.t:
Help developers and QA engineers during implementation when new questions arise.
Investigate unfamiliar areas independently rather than waiting for someone to explain.
Think about edge cases, dependencies, risks, and long-term maintainability.
Help reduce ambiguity around projects.
We care deeply about balancing business value, implementation effort, technical limitations, and platform strategy. We’re not fans of overengineering, but we also don’t like quick hacks that create bigger problems down the line.

s.h: We’ll be happy to bring you on board if you
s.t:
Have solid experience in business analysis within software development teams.
Understand how software development works end-to-end.
Know how to structure complex information and turn messy discussions into clear requirements.
Can stay focused on the core problem and avoid unnecessary complexity.
Are comfortable discussing implementation details with engineers and understanding technical constraints.
Can independently investigate unfamiliar functionality and connect dots across systems.
Care about the overall result, not only your direct area of responsibility.
Are proactive, curious, and comfortable working in an environment where not everything is perfectly documented.
Can adapt your communication style and analytical approach depending on the people and context involved.

s.h: It’d be a plus if you
s.t:
Can work with SQL.
Can read code well enough to understand what’s going on.
Have experience with technically complex systems or system analysis.
Have worked with billing, subscriptions, payments, or within other business-critical domains.

s.h: A few important things to know
s.t:
Our domain is genuinely complex. There’s a lot of history, many integrations, and a large codebase. You won’t learn everything in a month, and that’s okay.
We also continuously adjust processes and ways of working. If you like environments where everything is fixed and strictly defined forever, we’re probably not the best match. If you enjoy figuring things out, improving processes, and helping teams work more effectively together, you’ll likely feel very comfortable here.
Even though you’ll get the team’s full support and onboarding help, we really value people who are curious enough to explore things on their own.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Business Analyst to help shape the strategic transformation of our Financial Crime Compliance (FCC) and Market Conduct & Trade Surveillance (MCTS) capabilities within Legal & Compliance.
Working at the intersection of compliance, business, technology, architecture and data, you will shape strategic target states, assess current capabilities and translate business and control objectives into prioritised transformation roadmaps and actionable requirements. You will facilitate complex cross-functional decisions and provide clear recommendations to senior management.
You will act as the senior business-analysis and transformation lead for selected FCC and MCTS initiatives, shaping target states and roadmaps while working in close partnership with Compliance, Technology, Architecture, Data and Programme Management.

Lead the business definition of strategic target states, facilitating alignment across Compliance, Technology, Architecture and Data and ensuring that agreed target states are translated into actionable transformation plans.
Assess current capabilities and conduct gap analyses across processes, organisation, systems, architecture, data quality and governance, translating findings into prioritised transformation measures and investment considerations.
Define business and technology requirements and develop relevant use cases and options, including opportunities to improve data quality, reduce false positives, automate and scale alert handling, and strengthen monitoring and surveillance processes.
Translate target states into structured multi-year transformation roadmaps, defining priorities, milestones, dependencies, sequencing, responsibilities, investment considerations and key trade-offs across risk reduction, regulatory need, business value and delivery feasibility.

Facilitate cross-functional decision-making across business, technology and control functions, frame key options and trade-offs, and prepare concise recommendations and decision materials for senior management.

Define measurable transformation outcomes and success criteria, such as improved control effectiveness, reduced manual effort and false positives, better data quality and lineage, increased automation, and improved operational scalability.
Ensure traceability from regulatory, policy and control objectives through business requirements, solution design and implementation outcomes.

Demonstrated Financial Crime Compliance expertise combined with project and ideally consulting experience in the design and digital transformation of FCC solutions within a comparable financial-services environment.
Strong ability to work across business architecture, solution/enterprise architecture and data disciplines, translating business and control requirements into architectural, process and data implications.” Strong expertise in Financial Crime Compliance, with deep experience in one or more core domains such as AML/CTF, sanctions or PEP screening, and sufficient breadth to work effectively across adjacent FCC areas including tax compliance.Proven change and organisational capabilities, particularly stakeholder management and facilitation, Target Operating Model definition and the preparation of decision materials for senior management.
Strong conceptual and analytical capabilities, with experience translating strategic target states into prioritised multi-year roadmaps and implementation plans within complex transformation environments.
Fluent English and German are a must for this role.

Experience within Market Conduct, Trade Surveillance or comparable monitoring and surveillance environments; deep MCTS expertise is advantageous but not required where the candidate brings strong transferable FCC transformation experience.
Experience developing strategic concepts spanning Financial Crime Compliance, Legal & Compliance and wider banking transformation.
Familiarity with surveillance challenges such as false-positive reduction, alert management, data quality and the integration of relevant communications and market information.
Experience assessing investment requirements and prioritising transformation initiatives across three-to-five-year roadmaps.
Experience coordinating transformation plans with wider enterprise architecture, technology or bank-wide strategic programmes.

Who we are
Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.
As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

The Senior Business Analyst plays a key role in shaping the growth and success of Moniepoint’s payment products. You'll design, test, and implement strategies that improve user acquisition, boost retention, and elevate product engagement. This role blends deep quantitative analysis with collaborative, strategic thinking.

You'll partner with teams across the business to ensure our payment solutions meet real market demands and grow efficiently as we scale. Ultimately, you'll make sure our products not only attract users but also scale sustainably to create financial happiness for everyone.
Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.

Build, maintain, and scale self-service dashboards and custom visualisation tools.
Own end-to-end analytics for our growth products—from gathering data requirements and estimating opportunity sizes to designing experiments and conducting post-launch impact reviews.
Cultivate trusted relationships across teams, acting as a collaborative link between technology, business, and product.
Apply advanced mathematical and statistical modelling techniques (including A/B tests, multivariate testing, clustering, and supervised learning) to solve practical business problems that drive high-impact results.

3 to 4 years of professional experience (excluding academic projects and internships) in a quantitative analysis role within high-scale tech companies, tier-1 consulting firms, or investment banks with strong programming demands.
Excellent SQL skills (which we will test during our interview process).
Practical experience designing, running, and analysing experiments on digital products (such as A/B and multivariate tests).
Hands-on experience with popular visualisation tools like Tableau or Looker.
Experience applying statistical modelling and advanced analytics to deliver practical, product-shaping insights.
Strong skills in statistical programming (Python) and familiarity with tools like Pandas, SciPy, and Jupyter notebooks.
Clear, professional spoken and written English.

The Technology Systems Analyst plays a critical role in supporting and advancing CCI’s technology infrastructure and vendor ecosystem. They serve as CCI’s central hub for system integrations, vendor coordination, and technology risk oversight. This role bridges business needs, internal systems, external vendors, and internal employees ensuring platforms work together effectively without requiring in-house development.
The analyst proactively monitors system performance, integration health, and security posture, identifying risks and driving mitigation strategies across CCI’s technology ecosystem.

The analyst will also assist with internal audits and quality assurance processes, while proactively researching and recommending emerging technologies that align with CCI’s strategic goals.

The role requires strong systems thinking, with the ability to anticipate downstream impacts of changes, identify vulnerabilities, and drive mitigation strategies.

Systems Administration, Integration & Support
Administer and maintain core technology systems and platforms, ensuring reliability, stability, and performance
Map, document, and maintain visibility into system integrations, data flows, and dependencies across CCI platforms (e.g., CMS, LMS, CRM, finance systems)
Evaluate the downstream impact of system updates, configuration changes, and new features across integrated platforms
Validate and test integration outputs (data accuracy, timing, failure points) in collaboration with vendors
Troubleshoot cross-system issues and drive root-cause analysis across multiple platforms
Provide application support and guidance to staff, promoting effective and optimized use of systems
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand business needs and support system enhancements
Identify and reduce friction in system access, workflows, and support processes
Curate and maintain system documentation, including knowledgebase resources and process guides
Vendor Management, Security & Technology Governance
Serve as the primary liaison between internal stakeholders and vendors on integration design, changes, and issue resolution
Act as the technical point of accountability for vendor-delivered functionality, integrations, and system performance
Translate business requirements into clear technical expectations for vendors
Review vendor proposals, deliverables, and change requests for feasibility, impact, and alignment with system architecture
Identify risks related to cost, scope, timelines, technical approach, and security; escalate concerns as needed
Provide technical insight to support contract negotiations, renewals, and scope validation
Proactively monitor system security posture, vulnerabilities, and risks across platforms
Review and interpret third-party security reports (e.g., SOC 2, penetration tests, vulnerability scans) and translate findings into actionable insights
Assess vendor security practices and identify gaps relative to organizational expectations and compliance requirements
Collaborate with vendors to track and remediate vulnerabilities and ensure resolution
Stay informed on emerging security risks and recommend preventative controls
Support the development and enforcement of internal security standards, procedures, and incident response practices
Technology Strategy, Projects & Continuous Improvement
Support small to mid-sized IT projects and system change initiatives
Assist with internal audits, quality assurance reviews, and documentation of technology processes
Contribute to governance of emerging technologies, including AI tools and automation platforms
Research and evaluate new technologies to improve efficiency, integration, or service delivery
Recommend solutions that reduce manual work, improve data integrity, or enhance system connectivity
Drive workflow and process optimization with AI and other technologies

Experience working in multi-system environments with integrations across platforms (e.g., CMS, LMS, CRM, finance systems, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Egnyte Secure Cloud Storage, CRM/CMS platforms, financial systems (e.g., Sage Intacct), learning platforms (LMS), AI productivity tools (e.g., Copilot), and ticketing systems (e.g., Jira ITSM, Confluence Knowledgebase)

Experience leading or contributing to IT projects and change initiatives

Ability to work independently while collaborating across teams

The Product Business Analyst bridges the gap between business needs and engineering delivery, turning ideas, requests and requirements into clear, actionable work.
By bringing clarity to ambiguity, connecting work across Product and Platform Engineering and making sure teams have the information they need, the role helps reduce rework, improve delivery and build better software for our customers.

Discovery and shaping
Work with stakeholders to explore ideas, requests and feedback, clarifying the underlying problem, business need and intended outcome before work is defined
Explore the reasons behind requests before work is defined, ensuring relevant context and requirements are understood.
Challenge assumptions constructively, identify gaps and surface conflicting needs or unanswered questions early.
Identify and engage the right stakeholders to provide the information and decisions needed to shape clear requirements.
Turning needs into actionable work
Translate business needs into clear epics, features, user stories and acceptance criteria that give engineering teams sufficient context to progress work effectively.
Break down defined or moderately complex initiatives into clear, deliverable increments, working with Product and Engineering colleagues and seeking support on more complex work where needed,
Maintain accurate requirements and supporting context in Jira, including agreed scope, relevant decisions and material changes.
Keep requirements current as understanding or scope develops, working with relevant Product, Engineering and project colleagues to capture what has changed and why.
Question resolution during delivery
Remain closely involved during delivery as a point of contact for requirements-related questions and clarification.
Investigate ambiguity, work with the right stakeholders to resolve requirements questions and escalate more complex issues where needed so engineering teams can continue with clear direction.
Participate in refinement and planning discussions where business analysis input is needed to clarify scope, requirements or agreed decisions.
Maintain traceability from the original business need through agreed requirements and material changes to what is ultimately delivered.
Integrating product and platform work
Maintain awareness of relevant work across Product and Platform Engineering and identify dependencies, overlaps or potential impacts between teams.
Help shape requirements where product and platform changes need to work together, ensuring relevant dependencies and constraints are understood.
Flag where teams may be addressing the same problem, where proposed changes could conflict, or where work in one area creates an impact elsewhere.
Support effective handovers and cross-team working by ensuring teams have the requirements context and documentation they need.
Stakeholder engagement
Build constructive working relationships across Product, Engineering, QA, customer-facing teams and the wider business.
Translate engineering questions and constraints into clear language for business stakeholders.
Translate business needs and agreed intent into precise, actionable requirements for engineering teams.
Help stakeholders understand what has been agreed from a requirements perspective, what remains unresolved and where further input or decisions are needed.
Essential experience
Proven experience as a Business Analyst, or in a closely related analysis role, within software delivery.
Strong requirements elicitation and analysis skills, including the ability to work from incomplete or ambiguous information, identify gaps and challenge assumptions constructively.
Ability to translate business needs into clear, structured requirements, including epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria and supporting documentation.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage stakeholders at all levels and follow through to obtain the information needed to resolve ambiguity.
Experience working with Jira and Agile software delivery teams.
Experience working across multiple teams where shared dependencies, changes or overlapping requirements need to be understood clearly.
A good level of technical understanding, enabling effective conversations with engineers about scope, constraints, dependencies and trade-offs.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with good attention to detail and the ability to maintain clarity as requirements evolve.
Desirable experience
Experience working in a SaaS or platform engineering environment.
Familiarity with APIs, integrations and how platform capabilities can underpin product features.
Experience using analysis techniques such as process mapping or user journey mapping.
Exposure to software release processes and change management.
